about: What the parity harness leaves out when two engines' outputs of one job are not byte for byte the same: only the clock and entropy that reach the outputs, and where in a program's own code a crash happened, each named with the source line that writes it. Outputs equal after these masks are 'masked'; any other difference is 'different' (scripts/lib/parity/masks.ts, parity/README.md).

masks.why: The G-code header names the local time the file was written. The generator's name and version stay compared.
A 3MF's model can carry its creation and modification dates. Orca 2.4.2 writes them empty, so this mask finds nothing today; it stays in case a project that carries dates passes through.

masks.of: the entry of the same name without .md5
masks.why: The MD5 of a plate's G-code changes with the time in its header. It is masked only when each archive's MD5 is that of its own G-code entry, whose comparison then decides.

masks.source: deps_src/miniz (mz_zip_writer_add_mem stamps each entry with the time it was added)
masks.why: Each entry of a .gcode.3mf records the time it was written, in its local header and in the central directory.

A crash result names where the crash happened: the program's file name and the offset in it. Any two builds place their code differently, the oracle (sketch-orca-oracle.exe) among them, so the place differs while the crash is the same. The exception code and the stage stay compared.
